titolo: Trump Says Jensen Huang Came Up 'Briefly' With Xi. Why It Matters
angolo: Trump's 'briefly' answer about Huang to Xi, set against the three clocks now ticking on Huang: California's subpoena, the House hearing on Dec 1 and the China chip approvals
descrizione: Trump Says Jensen Huang Came Up 'Briefly' With Xi. Why It Matters. According to Reuters, Trump told Fox News he 'might have referred' to Huang's situation only briefly at dinner with Xi in Shenzhen. In the same 24 hours, California subpoenaed Nvidia and a House panel revealed 879,000 approved chip shipments to China. We separate what is confirmed from what is only reported.

scene.testo: A president says it came up only briefly. A tragedy, he calls it.
The man at the center resigned eight days ago.
Since its October peak, Nvidia has lost roughly $1.76 trillion in market value, according to CNN.
So what does 'briefly' really mean, when three clocks are ticking on Jensen Huang?

grafica.sotto: Trump, Xi and the fall of Jensen Huang

scene.testo: Here is exactly what Trump said.
It was Wednesday, on Fox News, on a show called The Ingraham Angle.
Reuters reports the president had just dined with Xi Jinping.
The dinner was in Shenzhen, China, at the APEC summit.
Trump says they spoke the whole evening, and mostly about artificial intelligence.
Then he was asked about Huang.
He added a second line, praising Huang.
He's such a brilliant man, Trump said, according to Reuters.
But the same quote contains something worth noticing.
Before 'briefly', Trump said 'we did not discuss it.'
Was it a formal discussion or a passing mention? Only Trump and Xi know what was said.
But first, who is the man everyone is talking about?
Thirty-three years after he co-founded it, Nvidia was valued at several trillion dollars.
Its chips powered the artificial intelligence boom.
He also became a regular visitor to the White House.
Reuters notes he voiced support for Trump's AI agenda and met him several times.
The goal: selling Nvidia chips to China.
In December 2025, Trump cleared the H200 chip for China.
It rolled back Biden-era limits and drew fierce criticism from China hawks.
Remember that decision. It comes back in a moment, with a number.
Because first, the story of how the crisis built.
Her name is Alice Huang. She is not related to Jensen Huang, according to CNBC and CNN.
She is a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company.
Megaspeed is under investigation over suspicions that it diverted restricted Nvidia chips to China, CNBC reports.
Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter, says US intelligence is trying to determine Alice Huang's ties to China's security ministry.
Those ties are reported, not proven.
Trump, asked directly, said he had not heard that she was a spy.
Then came the night of November twelfth.
CNBC cites a person familiar with the matter on how the board made its decision.
Nvidia announced on November twelfth that Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. Harvey Jones became first-ever board chair.
Interim CEO Colette Kress said she is committed to building on the foundation Huang created over 33 years.
Now the first clock: California.
On Thursday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia.
CNBC and UPI both report it.
He also asks whether Nvidia misled investors and the public about that risk.
Bonta told Politico the subpoena is the first step, according to UPI.

visivo.testo: Bonta told Politico the subpoena is the first step, according to UPI.

scene.testo: Nvidia is based in Santa Clara, California.
And the second clock is in Washington. It has a date.
On December first, Huang will appear for voluntary transcribed interviews before three House committees.
The panels are House Foreign Affairs, House Intelligence, and the Select Committee on China.
The interviews are transcribed and, per Axios, closed-door.
Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled for December second.
That is the statement of the committee chairmen Moolenaar, Mast and Crawford, not Huang's.
The Senate Banking Committee chairman, Tim Scott, has asked Huang to testify on December third.
And now, the third clock. The number I promised.
The House Foreign Affairs Committee disclosed it on Thursday.
The Commerce Department approved 879,000 chip shipments for Chinese firms, the committee says.

grafica.sopra: APPROVED FOR CHINA IN SIX MONTHS

scene.testo: The chips were Nvidia and AMD processors, approved between December 2025 and May 2026.
Approvals include 150,000 for Tencent, 75,000 for Alibaba, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD.
The committee noted that all four are on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.
A spokesperson said: 'Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China.'
Meanwhile, Nvidia's board has launched a search for a permanent CEO.
The board says it will consider both internal and external candidates.
So was it brief? Trump says so.

visivo.testo: So was it brief? Trump says so.

scene.testo: The man who led Nvidia for 33 years now faces three scrutiny fronts.
California's subpoena. Congress on December first. And the chip approvals disclosed by a House committee.
Huang has admitted, in an internal message to staff, that he was unfaithful to his wife. Investigators have not announced findings.
